subject: EdgeWave availability: fallback fingerprint & availability attribution
messages:
From: Naveen Rao <naveen@edgewave.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: sre+uptime@edgewave.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 03:12:00 +0000
Subject: Elevated error rate 2026-11-06 (request for attribution)

Jordan —

Quick note from our SREs: on 2026-11-06 between 02:15 and 02:48 UTC EdgeWave observed elevated 5xxs from a small subset of our POPs that matched the maintenance window we had scheduled for a cache invalidation push (maintenance-id: EW-MNT-789). Your status page shows the customer-facing latency bump but your SLA ledger attributes the entire 33-minute window to Redwood infrastructure rather than the third‑party maintenance.

Can you share how you’re correlating our maintenance notices with your probe data? Our procurement team needs to understand whether this will count toward an uptime credit. We’ve attached our internal timelines and the maintenance notice.

Thanks,
Naveen Rao
SRE Manager, EdgeWave
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Naveen Rao <naveen@edgewave.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 03:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Elevated error rate 2026-11-06 (request for attribution)

Looping in ops and billing to triage — I’ve attached our probe summary and the timeline we’ve been using for the SLA calculation. Initial automatic attribution marks the period as a partial service degradation rather than a full outage because 92% of requests still succeeded across other POPs, but the customer-facing error signal is non-trivial and the impacted region lines up with EdgeWave’s POPs.

Requests:
- Laura: can you confirm probe fanout distribution (per-POP weights) and whether our current apportionment rule (50/50 split when third-party maintenance overlaps) is still defensible given the observed fanout?
- Marissa: ops question — do we have a maintenance declaration mapping to your maintenance-id EW-MNT-789 in the ticketing system? If not, can we get one or ask EdgeWave for the maintenance window signed-off doc?
- Ben: finance — hold off on auto-credit until we confirm apportionment. We can offer a provisional goodwill credit if EdgeWave’s facts check out.

Attaching: edgewave_probe_summary.csv and downtime_timeline.png.

-Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Elevated error rate 2026-11-06 (request for attribution)

Jordan —

I pulled the probe logs. Summary: our global probe fanout to the affected customer cluster dropped by ~40% during 02:20–02:46 UTC as our routing engine rebalanced away from three POPs showing elevated 5xx. The successful request distribution indicates the degradation was highly localized (two POPs). Two notes on methodology:

1) Weighting: when an event is localized to a subset of POPs we currently weight attribution by request volume per-POP during the window. In this case that produces ~0.28 attribution to the third-party provider (EdgeWave) and ~0.72 to Redwood path because the majority of failed requests traversed Redwood-managed edges before hitting the CDN.

2) Fingerprint fallback: our runtime has a fallback fingerprint that marks requests retried via local cache hits as non-impacting for SLO if retry latency is <300ms. That reduces severity in cases where retries mitigate client-visible errors. Applying that rule here lowers the visible impact slightly but not enough to eliminate credit eligibility.

Proposal: schedule a 30‑minute joint replay (we have a prepared replay script) to reconcile per-request traces and agree on the apportionment. If EdgeWave provides a signed maintenance notice matching EW-MNT-789 we should apply the third‑party partial maintenance exclusion for the POPs they claim; otherwise we default to the weighted apportionment above.

-Laura
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:35:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Elevated error rate 2026-11-06 (request for attribution)

Adding ops context — we do not apply third-party maintenance exclusion unless all three conditions are met: (a) provider declares maintenance window in advance, (b) maintenance-id maps to the impacted POPs in our topology registry, and (c) our probes show a corresponding routing change (fanout delta) AND request failures originate after the provider’s maintenance start time.

In this incident: EdgeWave has provided EW-MNT-789 but it lists a global invalidation window 02:00–02:30 UTC; our error tail extends to 02:48 UTC due to retry/backlog effects. I recommend we:
- Run the joint replay (Laura’s suggestion) to reconcile per-request start times.
- If the replay shows failed requests initiated within 02:00–02:30 UTC and bound to EdgeWave POPs, exclude the overlapping portion up to 02:30 and apportion the remainder per Laura’s weighting.
- If the replay shows an independent failure chain after 02:30, we deny the exclusion and compute credit per our weighted model.

I’ve attached the maintenance-notice-789.pdf we received from EdgeWave. Ops can run a packet-level pull if legal signs off.

-Marissa
Director, Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Naveen Rao <naveen@edgewave.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Elevated error rate 2026-11-06 (request for attribution)

Naveen —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for sending EW-MNT-789. Internal takeaway: we all agree on the path forward — joint replay + trace reconciliation. High-level next steps from Redwood:

1) Schedule replay: Laura will run the prepared replay script and share a per-request CSV with timestamps and POP mapping (expected by EOD Wed 2026-11-11).
2) EdgeWave action: please confirm which POPs were part of EW-MNT-789 and supply any signed maintenance approvals; if you can export your CDN logs (request-id-level) that will speed reconciliation.
3) Interim customer-facing step: we will issue a provisional goodwill credit equivalent to 10% of the affected-window billing while we complete the apportionment. That does not prejudge the final calculation. Ben — please hold for final amount pending replay results.

If we can get the logs and replay results within 48 hours we’ll aim to finalize apportionment within one week. Appreciate the partnership on this — we want to ensure credits are fair and defensible for both sides.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
